subject: Discovery recap + technical readout — Quantum Bank latency & throughput commitments
messages:
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@quantumbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Subject: Discovery recap + technical readout — Quantum Bank latency & throughput commitments

Michael —

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and the technical highlights Marissa and I promised to capture after our call so we have one place to align on next steps.

Summary of pain & goals
- Customer-facing conversational assistant (fraud triage + account help) must maintain sub-200ms p95 inference for short prompts, p99 target ~350ms for normal traffic.
- Peak sustained throughput expected ~250 req/s for peak banking hours, burst up to ~450 req/s for brief spikes.
- Strict data controls: traffic must traverse VPC, audit logs retained 13 months, and keys managed via customer KMS.
- Model consistency: deterministic outputs for a small set of financial templates; require model pinning and rollback capability.

Technical constraints we captured
- Model: ~7B LLaMA-variant (8k context) finetuned on quantum-bank prompts. Preference for quantized int8 or 4-bit where QA passes.
- KV/prefix caching: client expects heavy prefix reuse across requests; caching important to meet latency targets.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn short prompts (<= 256 tokens), p99 <= 400ms across mixed workloads.
- Throughput profile: 70% short requests, 25% medium (256-2048 tokens), 5% long (>=2048).
- Region: us-west2 preferred for latency to customers.

Proposed deployment topology (initial)
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west2 (A100/H100 class), autoscale to maintain p95 SLO.
- Failover: Hosted Redwood API routed to eu-central (if regional capacity issues) with model-family fallback to 7B quantized variant.
- Networking: VPC peering + PrivateLink, TLS 1.3, customer-controlled KMS for keys.
- Observability: token-level cost slice, per-route latency histograms, and a 24/7 alert on p99 SLO breaches.

Attachments included: a short topology sketch, initial latency/cost estimate, and a draft mutual action plan for timelines and responsibilities.

Next steps
1) Marissa to confirm GPU sizing and initial benchmark plan (action: Marissa) — due Thu 2029-05-23.
2) Quantum Bank to share a 2k-row prompt set and representative traffic SEED for benching (action: Michael) — target by Mon 2029-05-27.
3) Ben to circulate the draft MPA and schedule a follow-up deep-bench session (action: Ben) — target by end of week.

If I missed anything or you want this written differently, say so and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll assume we proceed with the above and Marissa will post the benchmark plan tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + technical readout — Quantum Bank latency & throughput commitments

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing internally:

- Latency targets: we can tighten the p95 target to 120ms for short prompts if that significantly reduces cognitive load on the front-end team, but we understand cost implications.
- Data retention/audit: 13 months retention is correct. Also require immutable audit export capability for quarterly compliance snapshots.
- KMS: We will provide AWS KMS key ARNs; HSM integration is not required initially.
- Traffic pattern: our peak estimate of 250 req/s is conservative — engineering suggested preparing for 350 req/s in the first 90 days while we ramp.

Action items from us
- Share sample seed traffic and a 2k prompt set by 2029-05-27 (we’ll aim for EOD Friday).
- Infra will review VPC peering checklist from the topology PDF and revert with any firewall constraints (Infra owner: infra@quantumbank.com).

On the model side: our ML team prefers a 7B baseline but is open to exploring a 13B distilled variant if latency can be maintained with sharded KV and more aggressive quantization. Note: we will not accept >8s cold-start latencies.

Happy to join the bench session. Please include calendar invites.

—Michael Chen
Sr. Product Manager, Conversational AI | Quantum Bank
michael.chen@quantumbank.com
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 13:18:45 -0700
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@quantumbank.com>
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + technical readout — Quantum Bank latency & throughput commitments

Michael / Ben —

Thanks — I sketched an initial bench plan and a conservative GPU sizing approach. Attaching the quick topology PDF for clarity. Key technical notes below:

Bench plan summary (what we’ll run)- Baseline model: 7B LLaMA-variant, int8 quantized candidate + fallback int4 where accuracy holds.- Bench suites: (1) micro (<=64 tokens) latency p50/p95/p99; (2) mixed workload throughput soak (1 hour at target qps); (3) prefix-heavy cache hit-rate sensitivity test; (4) cold-start container spin / first-token latency.

Sizing assumptions (initial)
- For 250 sustained req/s mix above: 3 A100-80GB equiv workers with continuous batching + prefix cache should keep p95 under 150ms for short prompts.
- If you target 120ms p95, we’ll need either 1) H100-class workers (higher single-token throughput) or 2) increase workers to 4x A100 and tune batching window (cost trade-off).

Deployment notes
- Prefix caching: we’ll enable a shared KV cache layer in the Dedicated pool; recommend TTL 24h for prefix keys and warm-up prepop during customer peak windows.- Autoscaling: target CPU/GPU utilization + p95 as signals; can set a fast scale-up policy for burst windows to meet 450 req/s bursts.

Questions for Quantum Bank (short)
1) Do you have an existing SLO doc we should mirror for alerts & runbooks? (If so, share link.)
2) Any egress firewall restrictions that would block our bench nodes in us-west2 from hitting your test harness?

I’ll prepare a short script to run the microbench and post results in a shared drive folder. Ben — I put tentative dates for the bench run in the draft MPA.

—Marissa
